connection: a self-synchronized RemoteConnection (synchronized, idempotent close) written only on the single shield-session scheduler thread (connect, handleDisconnect); request threads and close() only read one snapshot, and the documented closed/connection volatile handshake makes connect() close a connection close() missed.

state: immutable DeviceState; every state.withX() read-modify-write runs on the single scheduler thread (connect, handleReady/handleDisconnect, and all RemoteListener callbacks marshalled through runOnScheduler); request threads only read.

lastScan: immutable BluetoothScan record (List.copyOf) stored by plain assignment at the end of scan() on HTTP request threads; lastScan() only reads; concurrent scans each publish a complete result, no read-modify-write.
state: immutable DeviceState read-modified-written only by readState()/publish() on the session's single virtual loop thread (poll, pollNow); request threads only read state().

running: every write (play, stop, stopIfCurrent) holds the player's monitor; active()/status()/require() take one lock-free snapshot of the immutable Running record, and status() only tears it down through synchronized stopIfCurrent.

connection: self-synchronized CastConnection (synchronized, idempotent close) written only on the cast-session scheduler thread (connect, Link.handleDisconnect); command threads and close() read one snapshot; closed/connection volatile handshake covers connect vs close.

receiver: immutable ReceiverStatus (List.copyOf) replaced wholesale on the scheduler thread; command threads (stop, load, customMessage, query) read a snapshot.

topology: immutable ZoneGroupState (List.copyOf) replaced wholesale by readTopology() from the poll loop and from grouping command threads; never modified in place, both writers store a fresh complete read.

installedApps (now in the Channel listener): immutable List.copyOf replaced wholesale by the HTTP client's listener thread; the Tizen session's threads only read it.

RailCache.ticker is assigned once in start() and only read (into a local, never read-modify-written) in stop(), both on Spring's lifecycle thread(s); the executor is thread-safe and volatile only publishes the reference. Declared with @SuppressWarnings on the field.

SsdpDiscovery.searchSocket is assigned once in start() (Spring init thread) and never replaced; read by the ssdp-search scheduler thread, and close() on the shutdown thread; DatagramSocket is thread-safe, volatile only publishes it.
SsdpDiscovery.notifySocket: assigned once in start(), read by listenPort() (request threads) and close(); MulticastSocket is thread-safe, no read-modify-write.
SsdpDiscovery.scheduler: assigned once in start(), never replaced or nulled; watch() (any thread) and close() only read it; ScheduledExecutorService is thread-safe.

cached holds an immutable SportsSettings record; every write (lazy load in current(), update()) and update()'s read-modify-write run under `lock`; lock-free readers (HTTP request threads, rail/schedule refresh threads) only need visibility. Declared on the field.

cached holds an immutable Base record replaced wholesale, and the new value comes from TMDB's /configuration response, not the old value. Concurrent poster() callers (rail refresh threads, search/item HTTP request threads) at worst both refresh and the last complete Base wins; nothing is lost. Declared on the field.

Operation.worker is set once by the worker thread before it runs the work and only read (into a local) by cancel() on the caller or close() thread to interrupt it; Thread is thread-safe, no read-modify-write.

WorkflowStore.snapshot is an immutable record (Map.copyOf/Set.copyOf) replaced wholesale; every read-modify-write happens under the `writes` ReentrantLock; request threads and ifCurrent() only read it.

Real race between HTTP request threads: submit()'s finally cancel() closed and cleared whatever attempt was current, so a submit finishing after a concurrent begin() killed the NEW attempt; two concurrent begin() calls could orphan a PairingSession (its TLS socket never closed). Now an AtomicReference: begin getAndSet (closes any attempt it displaces), submit compareAndSet(own, null), cancel getAndSet(null); regression test PairingServiceTest.aSubmitThatEndsAfterANewAttemptBeganLeavesTheNewAttemptInProgress (fails on the old code).

socket is now final: open() builds the inbound Channel listener first, opens the WebSocket, then constructs the connection with it, so no half-built connection is ever shared.

Real race: dropConnection()'s read-null-close ran on both the tizen-<id> scheduler thread (poll when the TV is off, lost) and close()'s caller thread with no common lock (a connection could be closed twice). Now AtomicReference: getAndSet(null) for drop/close, compareAndSet for lost() and the connect-vs-close path, so each connection is taken out and closed exactly once.
transport is only read and written on the ReconnectingPoller loop thread: volatile removed, documented as loop-confined.

Real race: close() (caller thread) read-nulled-closed the connection while lost() on the webos-<id> scheduler thread did check-then-null-then-close, no common lock (double close possible). Now AtomicReference: close getAndSet(null), lost and the connect-vs-close path compareAndSet, so each connection is closed exactly once.

Real race: events() (synchronized; rail refresh / request threads) replaced byItemId while forget() (setup request thread holding only SportsCalendars' lock) did copy-edit-write without it, which could overwrite a fresh index. Now AtomicReference: events() set(), forget() updateAndGet().
